key_insight: CAAMP is a large longitudinal Amish cohort built to uncover genetic and biological factors linked to cognitive aging, Alzheimer disease, and related late-life conditions.
clinical_relevance: The study may help identify inherited risk and protective factors that could improve future understanding, stratification, and prevention research for dementia and healthy aging.
method: Longitudinal follow-up of Amish participants in Ohio and Indiana
Clinical, cognitive, functional, and informant-based consensus adjudication of cognitive status
Integration of pedigree, genotype, whole-genome sequencing, biospecimens, and plasma biomarkers
evidence_signal: The cohort has enrolled 3,978 participants, with consensus cognitive data available for 2,928 and multiple age-related and biomarker datasets supporting ongoing evaluation.
watch_item: Because many participants lacked detailed cognitive evaluation at enrollment, some findings may be incomplete or not yet fully generalizable across the full cohort.
paper_title: A longitudinal study of age-related traits and cognitive function: The Collaborative Amish Aging and Memory Project (CAAMP)
